heroLine2: And still unable to do work.
heroSub: Between what a facility holds and what it can deliver, there is no agreed name. This index proposes one — and a taxonomy of the eighteen forms it takes across facility, IT and workload.
heroMono: Methodological benchmarking · Publicly accessible telemetry · No partnership implied
supportersNote: Built with support from the institutions backing the next generation of AI infrastructure.
problemTitle: Capacity is reported at the top and consumed at the bottom
problemLede: Megawatts contracted, racks installed, accelerators delivered. Those figures describe what exists. They do not describe what can be used.
problemBody: Between the two sits a set of constraints — electrical, thermal, topological, temporal and organizational — that keeps installed infrastructure from converting into work. This index proposes a single vocabulary for that distance.
chaptersLede: Each chapter is its own page, so it can be linked and cited on its own.

chapters.whatThisIndexDoesNotClaim: What this index does not claim

bannerText: Benchmarked against publicly accessible supercomputing telemetry — not private deployments.
bannerFoot: NERSC · Berkeley Lab · Perlmutter — no partnership implied
funnelLede: Seven steps from nameplate to useful output. The industry communicates the first three well. The last two decide whether the investment produced anything.
figureTitle: Capacity funnel — nameplate to useful output

01.name: Nameplate capacity
01.caption: Procurement and build-out. Equipment ordered but not yet racked and commissioned.

02.name: Installed capacity
02.caption: Grid connection and interconnection delay. Transmission lines take four to eight years in advanced economies.

03.name: Energized capacity
03.caption: Cooling and power distribution. Thermal envelope, UPS derating, branch and busway limits at rack level.

04.name: Supportable capacity
04.caption: Hardware availability and cluster topology. Nodes present but outside the eligible fabric, or not yet in the pool.

05.name: Allocatable capacity
05.caption: Scheduling and fragmentation. Free accelerators that cannot be assembled into a contiguous allocatable set.

06.name: Utilized capacity
06.caption: Queues, reservations and admission policy. Capacity held or waiting while demand is pending.

07.name: Useful output capacity
07.caption: Failed jobs, retries and idle allocation. GPU-hours assigned that produce no output.

funnelIdle: Hover a step to see what removes capacity before the next one.
gc1Body: A monotonic loss model. Each step removes capacity for a different reason — and the reasons do not share a metric.
gc3Body: The seven steps are defined. The measurement is not. Definitions and boundaries are open for comment before any figure is published.
disc: Proportions are illustrative. No measurement has been collected for any step.
